slots.name: destruction distance
slots.sentence: The deadly wall of water that descended from the mountains on the border between Nepal and Tibet caused destruction at least 62 miles downriver from the border in Nepal, an ABC News analysis of verified video and satellite images shows.

slots.name: landslide distance
slots.sentence: The flood was reportedly triggered by a landslide about 12 miles northeast of the Rasuwagadhi border post along the Nepal-China frontier, according to Nepal Disaster Management.

slots.name: landslide magnitude
slots.sentence: A 5.2-magnitude landslide was registered in Nepal on Wednesday, according to the U.S. Geological Survey.

slots.name: cliff height
slots.sentence: The initial location of the glacier was a cliff about 16,000 feet high.

slots.name: slope descent
slots.sentence: The debris avalanche, or landslide, slid down 6,000 feet on the slope, the USGS said.

slots.name: engulfed projects
slots.sentence: At least 11 hydropower projects were engulfed when a glacier collapsed into a river on the Nepal-China border on August 26, burying the entrances to the tunnels of these projects under debris and mud and cutting off those trapped inside.

slots.name: occurrence date
slots.sentence: The flooding, captured in dramatic video footage, occurred in the northern Rasuwa district along the border with Tibet at around 8:40 a.m. local time Wednesday, authorities said.
